summary: Lake Ontario light at the south-east tip of Prince Edward County: 1881 wooden tower, lantern removed 1959 when a skeleton tower took over the light; Parks Canada heritage lighthouse.

lens.note: 360-degree French lens installed 1909 in place of a catoptric (lamps and reflectors) apparatus; the old tower's lantern room was removed in 1959 (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: The 1881 Department description as LighthouseFriends prints it: 'a square wooden tower, 36 feet high, with keeper's dwelling attached'. Lantern removed 1959.
42 ft skeleton tower beside the old tower; active light (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Lightstation lies within Prince Edward Point National Wildlife Area, established 1978.

events.note: Dominion government appropriated $1,200 after a petition by captains of vessels and steamboats (LighthouseFriends)
Contract for construction awarded to John W. Fegan
Square wooden tower with keeper's dwelling, erected June 1881
Placed in operation in 1881; Thomas Fegan in temporary charge June to October
Fourth-order 360-degree French lens replaced the catoptric light (Department report 1909-10)
Discontinued by the Canadian government (LighthouseFriends; not checked in the Marine report)
Placed back in operation with the opening of navigation (LighthouseFriends)
Automated; characteristic changed from fixed red to flashing green
Skeleton tower erected beside the old tower to show a flashing white light; lantern room removed from the old tower
Prince Edward Point National Wildlife Area established
Designated a heritage lighthouse after a petition by Save Our Lighthouses
Government re-clad the tower; work finished in 2016 (Picton Gazette)

corrections.proposed: replaced 1959: skeleton tower took over the light; old tower's lantern removed
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says a 42 ft skeleton tower erected beside the old lighthouse in 1959 displays the flashing white light, and the lantern room was removed from the old tower. The light was not deactivated.

LighthouseFriends gives the 1959 skeleton tower's light as 46 ft above the surrounding water (about 14 m). The record's 7.0 m may describe the old tower, which no longer holds a lantern. A reviewer should check the CCG List of Lights entry (I429) first.

notes_for_editor: Vorce: the Department's 1909-10 salary table (scan 178, printed 171) and 1910-11 table (scan 269, printed 267) both read 'Nov. 21, 1902' and $240 for South Bay Point; both checked against the page images, matched by row. LighthouseFriends gives $200 ('the same amount that Keeper McIntosh had been earning'); the sources disagree and the story does not choose. Hudgin: the 1913-14 statement (scan 84, printed 77) gives 'W. Hudgins' for South bay point, appointed 15 June 1912, $260; the 1915-16 list keeps him at the station at $290. That fits LighthouseFriends' 1912 start for Waite J. Hudgin, but the initial and first name differ, so the link is by station and date only. The same 1913-14 list gives 'J. W. Hudgin' at False Ducks, appointed 3 May 1912, a different station. Ostrander (1927-41) does not appear in the corpus, which ends in fiscal 1923-24. Edward, point (L. Knauff, 1908) in the same 1913-14 list was not matched to this station. Height: LighthouseFriends and the 1881 Department description give the wooden tower as 36 ft; the record's 5.6 m structure height matches neither, and the 7.0 m focal height is unverified (the 1959 tower gives 46 ft, about 14 m, per LighthouseFriends). The CCG List of Lights was not read. Gazette 1959: the Picton Gazette says the lighthouse was 'decommissioned' in 1959; LighthouseFriends says the 1959 tower took over the light. The story states both. The 2015 date: LighthouseFriends dates the Heritage Lighthouse recognition to 2015; the Gazette places the Save Our Lighthouses petition 'until 2015' with designation soon after. The Coast Guard policy quoted by the Gazette is the paper's narrative of Seguin's account, not a quotation from a Coast Guard document. The Picton 'Miraculously...' sentence is narration, not Seguin's speech, and the story no longer quotes it. The 1900s-1910s list of 'South Bay point' was narrowed to the 1909-10 report, the one read as a footnote. Chronicling America has no 1880-1915 hit for 'Prince Edward Point'; no Canadian newspaper archive was searched, so the wrecks at the point are not documented. Carried over from the first pass and still true: a search-result snippet from the Register (not in the cached page) gives the combined lighthouse and keeper's residence as 7.8 m (26 ft); this is not verified and is not used in the story, and the record's structure height (5.6 m) matches neither. The record's CCG-derived 'Iso W 2s' conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 'flashing white' for the 1959 tower; the CCG List of Lights was not read. The Parks Canada DFHD page (id 14812) returned only a shell in fetch_text, so the Register text is from HistoricPlaces.ca. The range '10 miles' in the 1881 description is printed as miles with no unit note; the story gives it as printed, or leaves it out. The 1912 discontinuance and 1913 restoration are from LighthouseFriends; the 1912-13 Marine report was not checked for them. OCR of the 1913-14 keeper list splits the South bay point keeper as 'w hud gins'; the page image reads 'W. Hudgins' and the story quotes the image.
